I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Before running Q3, I computed Q2 the same way and got all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | consumer, 295,880,136 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 250 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | sw, 310,765,700 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u166@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 237 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 679,047 KRW |
| h. August → September growth | −2.9% |

Applying the definitions to the raw data didn't reproduce the Q2 values, so I tested two assumptions and kept the combination that matched:

- **Dates:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC. I converted it to Korea time (UTC+9) before deciding the quarter and month. Using UTC as-is gave different Q2 values.
- **Customers:** some emails appear on more than one customer id (`u120@ex.com` has 3). I counted customers by email rather than by id. Counting by id gives 280 for Q2 b instead of 234.
- **Segments:** names had inconsistent spacing and capitalisation (e.g. ` consumer`, `Enterprise `), so I trimmed them and made them lowercase before grouping.

The calculation script is `/work/scripts/an.py`.
